title: Needs vs. wants at a glance
alt: Two panels. Basic needs: groceries, housing, utilities, clothing, healthcare, transport, bus pass and savings. Wants: electronics, coffee, entertainment, fashion, streaming, hobbies, travel and dining out.
caption: Everyday items sorted into basic needs and wants.

title: Should I buy it now?
alt: Flowchart: if a purchase is essential, buy it from your needs budget. If not, wait 48 hours, then buy only if it still fits your wants budget; otherwise save the money.
caption: A decision guide for delaying non-essential purchases.

title: The 50-30-20 split
alt: Donut chart dividing monthly income into 50 percent needs, 30 percent wants and 20 percent savings, with example expenses for each part.
caption: How the 50-30-20 guideline divides monthly income.

title: The monthly budget cycle
alt: Five repeating steps in a circle: plan, track, review, adjust and save.
caption: Plan, track, review, adjust and save, then repeat each month.

title: A sample student month
alt: Bar showing a 500 dollar allowance split into rent 200, food 100, transport 40, books 30, wants 90 and savings 40.
caption: How a $500 allowance could be divided.

title: The 52-week savings challenge
alt: Bar chart growing from 1 dollar in week 1 to 52 dollars in week 52, for a total of 1,378 dollars saved.
caption: Save a little more each week and reach $1,378 in a year.

title: Student savings challenge
alt: Illustrated dashboard of savings ideas: buy used textbooks, cook at home, use free campus events and take public transport.
caption: Everyday ways students cut costs in each spending category.

title: Small expenses add up
alt: Growing circles: 4 dollars a day becomes 28 a week, 120 a month, 480 a semester and 1,460 a year.
caption: What a $4 daily habit costs over time.
